notes.rationale: The note explicitly describes flooding, detours and higher trip costs from February 24 through March 8, 2025. The week beginning March 10 is outside this window.
The note describes a temporary festival surcharge on Ahmedabad-Mumbai. The January 20-26 verification window is inferred; the source does not explicitly state exact event start and end dates.

The note describes a nationwide diesel-price increase starting the week of May 5, with costs rising roughly 5-7%. The source gives no end date. For verification, we conservatively accept this note only for the week beginning May 5 unless stronger evidence supports a wider period.
The note explicitly states that the affected routes are not included in this dataset. Reject it for every supplied route, despite the All Routes applicability label.

The note describes minor highway-maintenance delays for about one week but explicitly says costs were not significantly affected. The verification window is inferred and this note cannot justify a cost increase.

The note reports stable freight demand and no major disruptions. The verification window begins on the report date as a conservative assumption. This note cannot justify a cost increase and must not be applied to the Mumbai-Pune anomaly in the week beginning September 15.
The note describes road improvements after resurfacing but does not quantify their effect on freight costs. It cannot justify a positive cost increase.
The note reports normal operations and no significant disruptions. We conservatively limit its verification window to the week containing the note date. It cannot justify an increase.
The note confirms that normal route conditions returned after flood-related repairs. The one-week verification window is a conservative assumption. Recovery does not justify a new cost increase.

The note says vehicle-tracking compliance costs were absorbed by transporters without a rate change. The one-week verification window is a conservative assumption. This note cannot justify an increase.
